Let
\[
u=\frac{x_1+x_2+x_3}{\sqrt3}
\]
and use orthonormal coordinates \((a,b)\) on the plane \(x_1+x_2+x_3=0\). Then
\[
x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2=u^2+\rho^2,\qquad
\Delta(x)=-\frac1{\sqrt2}\rho^3\cos 3\theta .
\]
Hence
\[
I_n=\frac1{\sqrt2}\int_{\mathbb R}\int_0^\infty \rho^4 e^{-n(u^2+\rho^2)^4}
A\!\left(\frac{n\rho^6}{2}\right)\,d\rho\,du,
\]
where
\[
A(y)=\int_0^{2\pi}|\cos 3\theta|e^{-y\cos^2 3\theta}\,d\theta
=\int_0^{2\pi}|\cos\phi|e^{-y\cos^2\phi}\,d\phi .
\]

Scale \(u=n^{-1/8}t,\ \rho=n^{-1/8}r\), and put \(N=n^{1/4}\). Then
\[
I_n=\frac{n^{-3/4}}{\sqrt2}J(N),
\]
with
\[
J(N)=\int_0^\infty r^4F(r)A\!\left(\frac{Nr^6}{2}\right)\,dr,\qquad
F(r)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-(t^2+r^2)^4}\,dt.
\]

Put \(s=r^6\). Then
\[
J(N)=\frac16\int_0^\infty s^{-1/6}F(s^{1/6})A\!\left(\frac{Ns}{2}\right)\,ds.
\]
The Mellin transform of \(A\) is, for \(0<\Re z<1\),
\[
M_A(z)=\int_0^\infty y^{z-1}A(y)\,dy
=\Gamma(z)\int_0^{2\pi}|\cos\phi|^{1-2z}\,d\phi
=\frac{2\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma(z)\Gamma(1-z)}{\Gamma(3/2-z)}.
\]
Also
\[
L(z)=\int_0^\infty s^{-z-1/6}F(s^{1/6})\,ds
=6\int_0^\infty r^{4-6z}F(r)\,dr.
\]
Using polar coordinates in the \((r,t)\)-half-plane,
\[
L(z)=\frac{3\sqrt\pi}{4}\,
\frac{\Gamma\!\left(\frac{5-6z}{2}\right)}
{\Gamma(3-3z)}
\Gamma\!\left(\frac{3-6z}{4}\right),
\]
by analytic continuation.

The poles contributing up to order \(N^{-1}\) are \(z=5/6\) and \(z=1\). At \(z=5/6\),
\[
\operatorname{Res}_{z=5/6}L(z)=-\frac{\Gamma(1/8)}4,
\]
so
\[
J(N)=
\frac{2^{5/6}}{24}\cdot
\frac{4\pi^{3/2}\Gamma(1/8)}{\Gamma(2/3)}N^{-5/6}
+\cdots .
\]
This gives exactly the subtracted leading term
\[
\frac{\pi^{3/2}\Gamma(1/8)}
{3\,2^{2/3}\Gamma(2/3)}n^{-23/24}.
\]

For the next term, \(M_A(z)\) has residue \(-2\) at \(z=1\), while
\[
L(1)
=6\cdot\frac{\sqrt\pi}{8}\Gamma(-1/2)
\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\frac{\Gamma(\varepsilon/8)}{\Gamma(\varepsilon/2)}
=-6\pi.
\]
Thus the \(N^{-1}\) coefficient in \(J(N)\) is
\[
-\frac16\left((-2)\cdot 2\cdot L(1)\right)=-4\pi.
\]
Therefore
\[
I_n=
\frac{\pi^{3/2}\Gamma(1/8)}
{3\,2^{2/3}\Gamma(2/3)}n^{-23/24}
-\frac{4\pi}{\sqrt2}n^{-1}+o(n^{-1}),
\]
and hence
\[
\boxed{-2\sqrt2\,\pi}.
\]
